question: How much financial benefit is provided annually under PM-KISAN?
context: Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN) 1. Scheme Overview: PM-KISAN is a Central Sector Scheme launched by the Government of India to provide income support to all landholding farmers' families in the country. The scheme became operational on 1st December 2018. 2. Financial Benefits: Under the PM-KISAN scheme, an income support of Rs 6,000 per year is provided to all eligible landholding farmer families. The financial benefit is payable in three equal four-monthly instalments of Rs 2,000 each. The amount is directly transferred into the bank accounts of the beneficiaries through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) mode. 3. Eligibility Criteria: All landholding farmer families having cultivable landholding in their names are eligible for the benefit under the scheme. PM Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi (PM SVANidhi) 1. Background and Objective: PM SVANidhi is a Central Sector Scheme launched by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs to facilitate working capital loans to street vendors to resume their livelihoods affected by the COVID-19 pandemic. 2. Loan Tranches: The scheme provides collateral-free working capital loans in three progressive tranches: - First tranche: loan up to Rs 10,000 with a repayment tenure of 1 year. - Second tranche: upon timely or early repayment of the first loan, eligible for a loan up to Rs 20,000 with tenure of up to 18 months. - Third tranche: on timely repayment of the second loan, eligible for a loan up to Rs 50,000 with tenure of up to 36 months. 3. Interest Subsidy: - All superannuated or retired pensioners whose monthly pension is Rs 10,000 or more (excluding Multi Tasking Staff / Class IV / Group D employees). - All persons who paid Income Tax in the last assessment year. - Professionals like Doctors, Engineers, Lawyers, Chartered Accountants, and Architects registered with Professional bodies. 5. Mandatory Requirements: Beneficiaries must have an Aadhaar card. Aadhaar seeding with the bank account is mandatory for receiving the financial instalments. eKYC is mandatory for all PM-KISAN registered farmers. Ayushman Bharat - Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY) 1. Overview and Coverage: Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY is the world's largest health assurance scheme fully financed by the Government. It aims to provide a health cover of Rs 5,00,000 per family per year for secondary and tertiary care hospitalization to over 12 crore poor and vulnerable families (approximately 55 crore beneficiaries). 2. Benefit Package: The benefit cover of Rs 5 lakh per family per year is available on a family floater basis, which means that can be used by one or all members of the family. There is no restriction on family size, age, or gender of family members. Pre-existing conditions are covered from day one of the policy. 3. Scope of Services:
answer: Rs 6,000 per year in three equal instalments of Rs 2,000.

Families that own motorized two-wheelers, mechanized three or four-wheelers, motorized fishing boats, or mechanized agricultural equipment are excluded. Households with a member earning more than Rs 10,000 per month or paying income tax are also excluded. There is no restriction on family size, age, or gender of family members. Pre-existing conditions are covered from day one of the policy. 3. Scope of Services: PM-JAY covers up to 3 days of pre-hospitalization expenses and 15 days of post-hospitalization expenses such as diagnostics, medicines, and medical care. The services include approximately 1,949 treatment procedures across 27 specialties. Treatment is completely cashless and paperless at public and empanelled private hospitals across India. 4. Eligibility: Eligible households are identified based on the deprivation and occupational criteria of the Socio-Economic and Caste Census 2011 (SECC 2011) for rural and urban areas respectively. All landholding farmer families having cultivable landholding in their names are eligible for the benefit under the scheme. A landholding farmer family is defined as a family consisting of husband, wife, and minor children who own cultivable land as per the land records of the concerned State or Union Territory. 4. Exclusions: The following categories of beneficiaries of higher economic status are not eligible for benefits under the scheme: (a) All Institutional Landholders. (b) Farmer families in which one or more members belong to the following categories: - Former and present holders of constitutional posts. - Former and present Ministers, State Ministers, and former or present Members of Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, State Legislative Assemblies, or State Legislative Councils. Eligible households are identified based on the deprivation and occupational criteria of the Socio-Economic and Caste Census 2011 (SECC 2011) for rural and urban areas respectively. There is no enrollment process; families whose names are in the SECC database or National Food Security Act (NFSA) eligible lists are automatically entitled. An Ayushman card is generated to facilitate cashless treatment. 5. Exclusions: Families in rural areas that own motorized vehicles, motorized agricultural machinery, or Kisan Credit Cards with credit limit of Rs 50,000 or more are excluded. Government employees, households paying income tax, or households with non-agricultural enterprises registered with government are not eligible.
answer: No, families owning motorized vehicles are included.

question: What is the minimum assured monthly pension under PM-SYM?
context: (c) Monthly income should be Rs 15,000 or below. (d) Should not be an engaged member of EPFO, ESIC, or NPS (Government funded). (e) Should not be an income tax assessee. 3. Monthly Pension Benefit: Each subscriber under PM-SYM receives a minimum assured monthly pension of Rs 3,000 once they attain the age of 60 years. 4. Monthly Contribution: Contributions depend on the age of joining and the chosen pension amount. For example, for an entry age of 18 years, the monthly contribution is Rs 42 for a Rs 1,000 pension, and Rs 210 for a Rs 5,000 pension. For an entry age of 40 years, the monthly contribution is Rs 291 for a Rs 1,000 pension and Rs 1,454 for a Rs 5,000 pension. Contributions are auto-debited from the subscriber's savings bank account. 5. Benefits to Spouse and Nominee: After the death of the subscriber, the same monthly pension amount is payable to the spouse for life. Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-dhan (PM-SYM) 1. Mode of Payment: Pension is disbursed monthly directly into the beneficiary's post office or bank savings account, or via electronic benefit transfer. In remote areas, disbursement is allowed through cash at Panchayat offices.
answer: Rs 3,000 per month after attaining 60 years of age.

question: What is the maximum loan amount in the first tranche of PM SVANidhi?
context: PM Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi (PM SVANidhi) 1. Background and Objective: PM SVANidhi is a Central Sector Scheme launched by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs to facilitate working capital loans to street vendors to resume their livelihoods affected by the COVID-19 pandemic. 2. Loan Tranches: The scheme provides collateral-free working capital loans in three progressive tranches: - First tranche: loan up to Rs 10,000 with a repayment tenure of 1 year. - Second tranche: upon timely or early repayment of the first loan, eligible for a loan up to Rs 20,000 with tenure of up to 18 months. - Third tranche: on timely repayment of the second loan, eligible for a loan up to Rs 50,000 with tenure of up to 36 months. 3. Interest Subsidy: - Kishore: covering loans above Rs 50,000 and up to Rs 5,00,000 for enterprise consolidation and scaling. - Tarun: covering loans above Rs 5,00,000 and up to Rs 10,00,000 for mature small enterprises requiring business expansion. 3. Security and Collateral: No collateral or third-party guarantee is required for MUDRA loans up to Rs 10 lakh. Primary security consists of hypothecation of assets created through the bank loan. 4. Lending Institutions: Loans under PMMY are delivered by Public Sector Banks, Private Sector Banks, Regional Rural Banks (RRBs), Small Finance Banks (SFBs), Micro Finance Institutions (MFIs), and Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs). 5. Repayment Tenure: Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY) 1. Purpose and Scope: Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY) was launched on 8th April 2015 to provide collateral-free institutional credit up to Rs 10 lakh to micro and small non-farm, non-corporate enterprises for income-generating activities in manufacturing, processing, trading, and services. 2. Loan Categories: MUDRA loans are classified into three distinct categories reflecting the stage of development and funding needs of the beneficiary micro-unit: - Shishu: covering loans up to Rs 50,000 for entrepreneurs starting business or needing seed finance. - Kishore: covering loans above Rs 50,000 and up to Rs 5,00,000 for enterprise consolidation and scaling. The account can be opened with a minimum initial deposit of Rs 250. Subsequent deposits must be in multiples of Rs 50. The minimum deposit in a financial year is Rs 250 and the maximum limit is Rs 1,50,000 per financial year. Deposits can be made for a maximum period of 15 years from the date of opening of the account. 4. Interest Rate and Tax Benefit: The interest rate is determined by the Government on a quarterly basis. Investments qualify for tax deduction under Section 80C of the Income Tax Act up to Rs 1.5 lakh. The interest accrued and the maturity proceeds are completely tax-free (EEE status). 5. Maturity and Partial Withdrawal: The account matures after 21 years from the date of its opening or upon the marriage of the girl child after attaining 18 years of age.
answer: Up to Rs 10,000 with tenure of 1 year.

Background and Objective: PM SVANidhi is a Central Sector Scheme launched by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs to facilitate working capital loans to street vendors to resume their livelihoods affected by the COVID-19 pandemic. 2. Loan Tranches: The scheme provides collateral-free working capital loans in three progressive tranches: - First tranche: loan up to Rs 10,000 with a repayment tenure of 1 year. - Second tranche: upon timely or early repayment of the first loan, eligible for a loan up to Rs 20,000 with tenure of up to 18 months. - Third tranche: on timely repayment of the second loan, eligible for a loan up to Rs 50,000 with tenure of up to 36 months. 3. Interest Subsidy: - Kishore: covering loans above Rs 50,000 and up to Rs 5,00,000 for enterprise consolidation and scaling. - Tarun: covering loans above Rs 5,00,000 and up to Rs 10,00,000 for mature small enterprises requiring business expansion. 3. Security and Collateral: No collateral or third-party guarantee is required for MUDRA loans up to Rs 10 lakh. Primary security consists of hypothecation of assets created through the bank loan. 4. Lending Institutions: Loans under PMMY are delivered by Public Sector Banks, Private Sector Banks, Regional Rural Banks (RRBs), Small Finance Banks (SFBs), Micro Finance Institutions (MFIs), and Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs). 5. Repayment Tenure: Loans under PMMY are delivered by Public Sector Banks, Private Sector Banks, Regional Rural Banks (RRBs), Small Finance Banks (SFBs), Micro Finance Institutions (MFIs), and Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs). 5. Repayment Tenure: The repayment tenure is generally between 3 to 5 years, including a suitable moratorium period depending on cash flows. For accounts opened after 28th August 2018, the RuPay card comes with free inbuilt accidental insurance cover of Rs 2,00,000 (previously Rs 1,00,000), provided the card has been used at least once in 90 days. 4. Overdraft Facility: An overdraft facility of up to Rs 10,000 is available to eligible account holders after satisfactory operation of the account for 6 months. Only one overdraft facility is allowed per household, preferably to the lady of the house. 5. Direct Benefit Transfer: PMJDY accounts serve as the primary conduit for Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) of all government welfare subsidies under schemes like PM-KISAN, PAHAL (LPG subsidy), and MGNREGA.
answer: Up to Rs 20,000 with tenure up to 18 months. The benefit is restricted strictly to families owning a registered electric tractor.

Scheme Overview: Atal Pension Yojana is a periodic pension scheme targeted at all citizens in the unorganised sector, administered by the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) through the National Pension System (NPS) architecture. 2. Eligibility and Age: APY is open to all Indian citizens between the ages of 18 and 40 years who have a savings bank account. From 1st October 2022, any citizen who is or has been an income tax payer is not eligible to join APY. 3. Pension Options: Subscribers receive a guaranteed minimum monthly pension of Rs 1,000, Rs 2,000, Rs 3,000, Rs 4,000, or Rs 5,000 per month upon attaining the age of 60 years, depending on their contribution amount. 4. Monthly Contribution: During the receipt of pension, if the subscriber dies, the spouse is entitled to receive 50% of the pension as family pension (Rs 1,500 per month). Family pension is applicable only to the spouse. 6. Required Documents: To enroll, the individual needs an Aadhaar card and a savings bank account or Jan Dhan account with IFSC code. - All superannuated or retired pensioners whose monthly pension is Rs 10,000 or more (excluding Multi Tasking Staff / Class IV / Group D employees). - All persons who paid Income Tax in the last assessment year. - Professionals like Doctors, Engineers, Lawyers, Chartered Accountants, and Architects registered with Professional bodies. 5. Mandatory Requirements: Beneficiaries must have an Aadhaar card. Aadhaar seeding with the bank account is mandatory for receiving the financial instalments. eKYC is mandatory for all PM-KISAN registered farmers. Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme (IGNOAPS - NSAP) 1. Scheme Purpose: IGNOAPS is a non-contributory component of the National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP) administered by the Ministry of Rural Development, providing monthly social pensions to senior citizens living below the poverty line. 2. Eligibility: (a) The applicant must be 60 years of age or older. (b) The applicant must belong to a household living below the poverty line (BPL) according to the criteria prescribed by the Government of India. 3. Central Assistance Amount: - For persons between 60 and 79 years of age, the Central Government provides assistance of Rs 200 per month. - For persons who are 80 years of age and above, the Central Government assistance is Rs 500 per month.
answer: No, income tax payers are eligible to join APY from 1st October 2022.

question: What is the eligible age group for PMJJBY?
context: Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-dhan (PM-SYM) 1. Scheme Purpose: PM-SYM is a voluntary and contributory pension scheme for unorganised workers for ensuring old age protection. It is administered by the Ministry of Labour and Employment and implemented through Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) and Common Services Centres (CSCs). 2. Eligibility Criteria: (a) The applicant must be an unorganised worker (such as street vendors, head loaders, brick kiln workers, cobblers, rag pickers, domestic workers, rickshaw pullers, landless labourers, agricultural workers, construction workers). (b) Entry age must be between 18 and 40 years. (c) Monthly income should be Rs 15,000 or below. (d) Should not be an engaged member of EPFO, ESIC, or NPS (Government funded). Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY) 1. Purpose and Coverage: PMJJBY is a government-backed life insurance scheme providing life cover for death due to any reason. The life insurance cover provided is Rs 2,00,000. 2. Eligibility: Individuals aged between 18 and 50 years having a savings bank account or a post office bank account are eligible to join the scheme. The cover terminates when the subscriber reaches 55 years of age. 3. Premium: The premium is Rs 436 per annum per member, which is auto-debited from the subscriber's bank account in a single instalment on or before 31st May each year for the annual coverage period from 1st June to 31st May. 4. Lien Period: A lien period of 30 days is applicable from the date of enrollment. There is no restriction on family size, age, or gender of family members. Pre-existing conditions are covered from day one of the policy. 3. Scope of Services: PM-JAY covers up to 3 days of pre-hospitalization expenses and 15 days of post-hospitalization expenses such as diagnostics, medicines, and medical care. The services include approximately 1,949 treatment procedures across 27 specialties. Treatment is completely cashless and paperless at public and empanelled private hospitals across India. 4. Eligibility: Eligible households are identified based on the deprivation and occupational criteria of the Socio-Economic and Caste Census 2011 (SECC 2011) for rural and urban areas respectively. The identification and selection of beneficiaries under PMAY-G is done through Socio-Economic and Caste Census (SECC) 2011 data, finalized by the Gram Sabha. Families that own motorized two-wheelers, mechanized three or four-wheelers, motorized fishing boats, or mechanized agricultural equipment are excluded. Households with a member earning more than Rs 10,000 per month or paying income tax are also excluded.
answer: 18 to 50 years of age.

question: What is the maximum loan under Shishu category of PM Mudra Yojana?
context: Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY) 1. Purpose and Scope: Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY) was launched on 8th April 2015 to provide collateral-free institutional credit up to Rs 10 lakh to micro and small non-farm, non-corporate enterprises for income-generating activities in manufacturing, processing, trading, and services. 2. Loan Categories: MUDRA loans are classified into three distinct categories reflecting the stage of development and funding needs of the beneficiary micro-unit: - Shishu: covering loans up to Rs 50,000 for entrepreneurs starting business or needing seed finance. - Kishore: covering loans above Rs 50,000 and up to Rs 5,00,000 for enterprise consolidation and scaling. PM Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi (PM SVANidhi) 1. Background and Objective: PM SVANidhi is a Central Sector Scheme launched by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs to facilitate working capital loans to street vendors to resume their livelihoods affected by the COVID-19 pandemic. 2. Loan Tranches: The scheme provides collateral-free working capital loans in three progressive tranches: - First tranche: loan up to Rs 10,000 with a repayment tenure of 1 year. - Second tranche: upon timely or early repayment of the first loan, eligible for a loan up to Rs 20,000 with tenure of up to 18 months. - Third tranche: on timely repayment of the second loan, eligible for a loan up to Rs 50,000 with tenure of up to 36 months. 3. Interest Subsidy: - Kishore: covering loans above Rs 50,000 and up to Rs 5,00,000 for enterprise consolidation and scaling. - Tarun: covering loans above Rs 5,00,000 and up to Rs 10,00,000 for mature small enterprises requiring business expansion. 3. Security and Collateral: No collateral or third-party guarantee is required for MUDRA loans up to Rs 10 lakh. Primary security consists of hypothecation of assets created through the bank loan. 4. Lending Institutions: Loans under PMMY are delivered by Public Sector Banks, Private Sector Banks, Regional Rural Banks (RRBs), Small Finance Banks (SFBs), Micro Finance Institutions (MFIs), and Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs). 5. Repayment Tenure: Loans under PMMY are delivered by Public Sector Banks, Private Sector Banks, Regional Rural Banks (RRBs), Small Finance Banks (SFBs), Micro Finance Institutions (MFIs), and Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs). 5. Repayment Tenure: The repayment tenure is generally between 3 to 5 years, including a suitable moratorium period depending on cash flows.
answer: Up to Rs 50,000.
